A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DTop-p MoE. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model and diffusion-transformer experiments, benchmark scores, scaling investigations, and routing ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds an experimental comparison involving layer-wise DTop-p.

M1.justification: Section 4.2.3 adds a variant with independent PI controllers and probability thresholds for each layer, replacing global budget sharing with per-layer targets. The default routing procedure, dynamic routing normalization, and training losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use DCLM training data, C4 validation, the same 13 downstream NLP benchmarks, and internal image/image-text data for DiT experiments. The layer-wise experiment changes routing configuration within existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 9 adds layer-wise DTop-p as a comparator to the default global method alongside Top-k and fixed-threshold Top-p. The existing Dense, Top-k, Top-p, and Top-k-with-DRN comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The added layer-wise comparison sets every layer's target to the same eight-expert budget, explicitly matching Top-k at the layer level. Existing experiments retain their data splits, evaluation metrics, few-shot settings, training budgets, and model configurations.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 9 adds an analysis of global versus independent per-layer budget control, comparing loss, thresholds, and activation tracking. Existing component, controller, optimizer, weight-tying, and loss ablations are retained, often relocated. Distribution-shift discussion does not introduce a robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same means and standard deviations of expert activation. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for benchmark performance.

E6.justification: Main benchmark scores remain unchanged, including Table 2 averages of 49.0 for Top-k and 50.9 for DTop-p. New Figure 9 reports near-target activation within individual layers and slightly worse validation loss for layer-wise DTop-p than global DTop-p. Table 10 tabulates endpoints from existing loss curves.

T1.justification: New Equations 8–9 formalize layer-specific activation statistics, targets, errors, and threshold updates, introducing independent budget constraints. Existing routing and loss mathematics is retained or renumbered; no convergence theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The introduction adds the layer-wise variant for explicit per-layer compute control to the stated contributions. The central claims about PI-controlled Top-p routing, normalization, performance, and scaling remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the layer-wise variant's validation disadvantage as the cost of restricting cross-layer compute allocation. Appendix H adds explanations of synchronization overhead, compatibility with load balancing, controller behavior under distribution shifts, and baseline scope. Existing scale and controller-calibration limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix H adds guidance on obtaining controller statistics from token-expert assignments and potentially fusing their all-reduce. However, v2 Appendix J removes v1 Appendix G's promise to release source code and training scripts upon publication. Hardware and hyperparameter disclosures remain; actual code availability is not established.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Qu et al. (2026), Wang et al. (2025), and Zou et al. (2025), and removes Tang et al.'s Pangu Ultra MoE reference. It also explains why expert-choice routing is outside the comparison scope and zero-compute experts are complementary. Core research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, experimental narrative, and conclusion are substantially rewritten or condensed. v2 introduces main-text Related Works and Additional Investigations sections, reorganizes scaling and loss discussions into appendices, and condenses the former ethics appendix into an Impact Statement.

P2.justification: The main text changes to a two-column layout with substantially reformatted tables and resized plots. The overview moves earlier; scaling tables and several ablation figures move to appendices. Figures 3–4 gain annotations, and v2 adds the multi-panel Figure 9 and loss-summary Table 10.

improvement.justification: The layer-wise variant and Figure 9 add a useful tested alternative and clarify the trade-off between validation loss and per-layer budget control. Deployment explanations improve understanding, although removing the code-release commitment weakens reproducibility assurances. With the principal empirical findings unchanged, these additions provide a limited net improvement.
